title: US Regulators Block Proposal to Cut AI Data Center Power
summary:
Federal officials have dismissed a petition that would have authorized electricity providers to disconnect artificial intelligence hubs during periods of peak grid stress. The decision by U.S. regulators to block the proposal comes as the energy requirements of AI facilities create growing instability for utility providers attempting to maintain regional power grids during emergencies.

The regulatory move follows warnings from Mississippi utility Entergy, which told Amazon its data centers would face disconnects during periods of high demand. In response, AWS developed Project Falcon, a system allowing Entergy to transition facilities to backup power without contacting the company. Synergetic CEO Mike Sloan stated that data centers must accept curtailment and maintain a "toolbox" to handle such risks.

selectedTweets.text:
The power grid just became the AI bottleneck. The Information reports Mississippi's Entergy told Amazon it would start kicking Amazon's data centers off the grid at peak times, a previously unreported warning that prompted AWS to change how those sites switch to backup power.

Amazon's answer is Project Falcon. Now the utility can switch the sites to backup power on its own, without contacting AWS. Falcon was built for Mississippi and may roll out elsewhere in the U.S. As Synergetic CEO Mike Sloan put it: "[Data centers] have to accept some curtailment, which means then the data center has to have a toolbox that can handle that risk."
